problem_statement: Astroship is the marketing site for Ferrolane, an intermodal rail-yard slotting platform, built on Astro and Tailwind CSS: a homepage with a hero, feature and logo strips and a call to action, a Pricing page, an About page, a Contact page, and a 'Field Notes' blog at /blog that lists the team's articles, with individual article pages under /blog/<slug>, all wrapped in a shared Navbar (Platform / Pricing / About / Field Notes / Contact) and a shared Footer. The Field Notes blog hosts its own reading tool: a 'Browse by topic' category filter that sits above the article feed. It is a labelled row of the desk's four standing topic chips (Operations, Reliability, Playbooks, Field Reports) plus an All chip, and a live readout that reports how many of the nine articles are showing for the chosen topic, in the form 'Showing N of 9 . <Topic>'. The filter is promoted on both surfaces that list posts: the Field Notes index (/blog/) and the homepage's Latest-from-the-Field-Notes area. Ship the Browse-by-topic filter so it (1) appears above the article feed on the Field Notes index AND on the home page, (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the Ferrolane blue/slate styling (rounded pill chips keyed to the theme tokens, a tidy card grid) rather than an off-palette slab or an overlapping pile of cards, and (4) keeps the readout in sync so a reader who clicks the Operations chip sees the feed narrow to the three Operations articles and the readout update to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Operations' — it must re-read the live matched set, not show a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, existing pages, the article pages, the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Browse by topic' category filter above the article feed so it renders on BOTH the Field Notes index (/blog/) and the home page's Latest-from-the-Field-Notes area (a shared component, not a per-page copy).
The filter shows a 'Browse by topic' label, a chip row of All plus the four standing topics (Operations, Reliability, Playbooks, Field Reports), and a live 'Showing N of 9 . <Topic>' readout.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the filter in the Ferrolane blue/slate language (rounded pill chips keyed to the theme tokens, a legible active chip, a tidy card grid), not an off-palette slab and not a collapsed pile of overlapping article cards.

Wire the chip clicks so that clicking a topic (for example Operations) re-filters the feed to the matching articles AND re-syncs the readout to 'Showing N of 9 . <Topic>' (for example 'Showing 3 of 9 . Operations'); marking the chip active is not sufficient — the readout must re-read the live matched set, not a stale captured value.
Preserve navigation (Platform / Pricing / About / Field Notes / Contact), the footer, the existing pages, the article pages and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the Browse-by-topic filter as a shared component so a single source of truth reaches the Field Notes index and the home page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The filter must adopt the Ferrolane theme tokens (the blue-600 accent, slate text, rounded pill chips, an uppercase small-caps label, the same margins/padding and font family) so it reads as part of the site; the active chip must be legible (high-contrast blue fill / white text), and the filtered feed must stay a tidy card grid, not a negative-margin pile.
Keep the readout in sync with the CURRENT filter selection after every click by recomputing the visible count from the matched set, so it can never go stale relative to the shown articles.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, existing pages, the article pages or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the homepage hero, feature strips and Latest-from-the-Field-Notes area across viewports, and carry the Browse-by-topic filter on the home page (D2 cross-page presence).

desktop_blog, mobile_blog and tablet_blog frame the Browse-by-topic filter and article feed on the Field Notes index across viewports; the reference keeps 0 overflow and a tidy grid, the negative controls overflow on mobile and (for the bad leg) collapse into overlapping cards.
desktop_post, desktop_about, mobile_about and desktop_contact protect the existing article, About and Contact reading surfaces.

blog_filter_operations clicks the Operations topic chip on the Field Notes index; the feed must narrow to the three Operations articles and the readout must re-sync to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Operations' (the interaction terminal state).
The mobile blog state (mobile_blog) is the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width negative controls overflow.

change_completion: The Browse-by-topic filter is present above the feed on BOTH the Field Notes index and the home page (the shared component reaches both routes).

After clicking the Operations topic chip on the Field Notes index, the feed narrows to the three Operations articles and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Operations' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 9 of 9 . All topics'.
design_consistency: The filter on the blog states matches the reference's blue/slate styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a legible active chip and a tidy card grid, not an off-palette slab or an overlapping pile.
The filter adopts the Ferrolane theme tokens and pill-chip idiom so it reads as part of the site across every surface.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_blog and tablet_blog keep the filter and article feed readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Platform / Pricing / About / Field Notes / Contact), the footer and the existing pages remain present and functional.
The existing article/about/contact content, the Astro build and the site's images are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add the blog's own on-brand 'Browse by topic' category filter across the post-listing surfaces with a live count readout, while keeping the navigation, existing pages and Astro build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Astro + Tailwind business marketing site with a shared Navbar/Footer, a homepage with hero/feature/CTA sections, Pricing/About/Contact pages, and a 'Field Notes' blog index plus article routes, using Tailwind CSS theme tokens and local assets
metadata.selected_repo_reason: surjithctly/astroship is a runnable Astro 5 + Tailwind 4 business marketing site with a real 'Field Notes' blog; it builds to static output offline and hosts a natural experience-continuity add on the blog's OWN post-listing category filter spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page presence, filtered-feed layout, and chip-click count wiring.

author_notes: slot_247 reassigned off the shared StartBootstrap clean-blog repo (kept by the lower slot_105) and rebuilt to a genre-native L4 on the surjithctly/astroship Astro marketing site with a 'Field Notes' blog. The lever is the blog's OWN post feed and its native 'Browse by topic' category filter (All plus four standing topics over nine real Field Notes articles, with a live 'Showing N of 9 . <Topic>' readout), not a bolted-on metric rail. Each article carries a real category (Operations, Reliability, Playbooks, Field Reports) added to the Astro content schema and frontmatter. The filter is hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the chip row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px phone; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Browse by topic' filter must be promoted on both the Field Notes index and the home page; reference promotes it on both, baseline and bad only on the blog index so both fail the home-page presence assertion. Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered feed collapses — the article cards are pulled together with negative margins so they shingle into an illegible overlapping pile and the active chip is near-white text on a near-white fill — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad chip click flips .is-active and hides cards but rewrites the readout from a label snapshotted in a closure, so after the Operations click the readout stays 'Showing 9 of 9 . All topics'. Four leg-varying files (src/components/PostFilter.astro, src/styles/postfinder.css, src/pages/index.astro, src/pages/blog.astro) live in suggested_files; the article content, the content-schema category taxonomy and the local cover asset are shared byte-identically across legs. Built offline as static Astro output served by a static file server, with the cover image local and no network calls; that infrastructure is identical across legs.
